welcome.title: Welcome to Ten10
welcome.description: If you'd like to learn the system, you can start a tour now.
welcome.restartBefore: If not, you can always start it from the
welcome.restartAfter: at the top, or from Settings.
welcome.skip: I'll look around on my own

tour.homeIntroDescription: Home has three cards for the period you pick — income, expenses, and donations — and a Tithe balance card that tracks the tithe over time. We'll meet them, then add a new transaction.
tour.dateRangeDescription: These buttons show income, expenses, and donations for the selected period — the tithe balance stays the same.
tour.titheBalanceDescription: Shows the tithe still left to give. A minus is good news — you have already given more than required and have a credit.
tour.openingBalanceDescription: If you already have a tithe balance from a notebook or Excel, you can add it here easily. This is a one-time transaction.
tour.cardQuickAddDescription: The plus on Income, Expenses, or Donations opens the add-transaction form with that type selected.
tour.continueToFormDescription: Now we'll open the add-transaction form and add transactions as needed.
tour.formIntroDescription: Here you can add every type of transaction. Type, amount, date, and description are enough to save — and the more detail you add, the better you can manage household finances.
tour.formImportDescription: Have many transactions in Excel or from the bank? Import them here from a CSV or Excel file in one go.
tour.formBasicsDescription: Choose the type — income, expense, or donation — then enter an amount (in any currency), a date, and a short description.
tour.flagsDescription:
The buttons change with the transaction type:

  • Income — «Exempt from tithe» skips the calculation. «Calculate chomesh» takes 20% instead of 10%.
  • Expense — «Recognized expense» reduces the obligation by 10% of the amount (or 20% for chomesh). A regular expense does not affect it.
  • Donation — a regular donation reduces the balance. «Not from tithe funds» is recorded without reducing the obligation.
tour.recurringDescription: If this is a repeating transaction, this saves a new standing order in the Standing orders table. The transaction is not created immediately — Ten10 creates it automatically on the day you chose, for the period you set.
tour.liveBalanceDescription: After you save the transaction, you will see the summary cards on the side update.

success.title: Your first transaction is saved
success.description: On Home, below the cards, there is a Monthly summary. Contact opens a message to a rabbi or the development team.

checklist.title: Getting started
checklist.description: Two short steps to see Ten10 at work.

pageTour.ariaLabel: Start a tour of this page

importTour.introDescription: Import a batch of transactions from a CSV or Excel file. The flow is prepare, upload, mapping, and review. Only what you approve at the end is added to the table.
importTour.stepsDescription: Prepare, upload, map columns, and review. In review you choose what to import. You can go back at any stage. Nothing is saved before the final approval.
importTour.templateDescription: You can download an empty Ten10 template and fill it with transactions — column mapping will happen almost by itself because the file is built for the app. It is optional; you can also upload your own file with clear headers.
importTour.uploadDescription: Drop a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file here, or click to choose one. After the file is read, you move on to mapping.
importTour.mappingDescription: Next you match each column in the file to a Ten10 field.
importTour.reviewDescription: You see a preview of the transactions, fix errors, and mark what to import. Duplicate or suspicious rows are flagged first.
importTour.approveDescription: Only after your final approval are the transactions added to the table. Until then you can go back, fix rows, or cancel.
